messages:
sara: FYI — partner 'EdgeBox' is sending usage events with a ~45s clock skew vs their stated UTC seconds. This is causing our hourly rollups to put some events in the previous hour and some in the next hour, which creates tiny credit drift. Anyone else seeing weird negative/positive deltas in nightly reconcile?

liam: saw a spike in the reconcile summary at 03:00 UTC this morning. diffs small but consistent. digging now. :mag_right:

ana: do we round to minute or second when bucketing? i thought we floor to the hour by event_ts but maybe the ingest pipeline does a minute-bucket first.

liam: we ingest raw then write to kafka partitioned by partner+hour_key where hour_key = to_char(bucket_start_ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYYMMDDHH24'). downstream aggregation assumes event_ts within same hour_key. if event_ts is 59s before hour, but arrives after the cut we still put it into prior hour_key.

sara: that lines up — partner TCP replay plus their clock skew == events crossing the hour boundary. consequences: partner sees credits X, we see X +/- a tiny delta because their reporting window uses event_ts rounding differently.

raj: quick sample i pulled from raw events: ```
{
  "event_id": "evt_9a3f",
  "partner_id": "edgebox",
  "event_ts": "2026-08-17T02:59:15.921Z",
  "received_ts": "2026-08-17T03:00:03.102Z",
  "usage_units": 120
}
```
note event_ts is inside 02:00-02:59UTC but received after 03:00 cutoff.

ana: ah ok. partner claims they align to the minute (floor), but their SDK might be producing wall time with NTP drift. Can we tolerate +/-1 minute? current ledger is strict by hour.

liam: tolerances: our billing contract with marketplace partners expects event_ts-based attribution. but we also support ingestion-time backfill window of 24h. main issue is the automated reconciliation that flags >0.01% deltas and opens tickets. small noise is noise but makes noise for ops.

sara: proposal: 1) short-term: adjust aggregator to apply a 120s jitter-tolerant bucketing when partner=EdgeBox (config flag) so we coalesce events within a 2-minute window around the hour boundary into the hour derived from event_ts. 2) medium-term: ask partner to fix SDK clock sync and add heartbeat TTL. 3) run a one-off re-run/backfill for last 7 days for EdgeBox to remove noise from reconcile.

raj: implementation note: change would be in ingestion service config: "hour_window_tolerance_seconds": 120 for partner edgebox. patch is small but will need canary.

ingest-bot: deploy queued: patches/ingest-hour-window-tolerance @eng-infra (canary) — ETA 2h.

liam: canary checklist: - apply config to staging edgebox partition - run integration test with synthetic events straddling boundary - verify reconcile alert suppression for that partner - confirm no downstream time-series cardinality explosion

ana: for the backfill i can run the existing hourly-aggregator in backfill mode with the new tolerance flag and write to backfill-ledger namespace. i estimate 30m for 7 days at current throughput.

sara: sounds good. @raj can you draft the message to partner asking them to verify NTP sync and adopt SDK fix? include sample payload and recommended TTL header. keep it non-blaming and actionable.

raj: on it. will send a short email and include examples + ask for a small test run. cc: account team.

liam: one more thing — let's add a reconciler rule to ignore diffs < 0.02% for partner edgebox while we do the backfill to avoid pager noise. we should log suppressed diffs for audit.

sara: agreed. I'll create the ticket with owner mapping: liam -> ingestion patch, ana -> reconciliation rule, raj -> partner comms, nana -> backfill run. Target: staged deploy + backfill + partner message today EOD UTC.

ana: thumbs up. I'll post a short runbook in #partnerships-runbooks once backfill command and flags are finalized.

raj: draft to partner (copied to thread): "Hi EdgeBox team — quick heads-up: we've observed some usage events crossing hour boundaries due to clock skew on your side. To avoid small billing deltas on our reconcile, could you: 1) confirm NTP sync on SDK hosts; 2) include an x-sdk-ts-ttl header (suggest 300s) on batched payloads; 3) run the attached test payloads and share results. We'll also run a harmless backfill on our side to smooth historical noise. Happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful."

sara: love it. please send and paste thread link here after sending.

ingest-bot: deploy started: patches/ingest-hour-window-tolerance -> canary (ingest-staging-edgebox).

liam: canary looks good so far. no extra cardinality, suppressed reconcile alerts for the test window.

ana: backfill complete for 7-day window. wrote to backfill-ledger namespace. diffs reduced to baseline.

raj: partner replied: they were on an older image with a bug in the SDK timestamp math. they're rolling patch and will enable NTP. thanks from their ops lead.

sara: win. follow-ups: - PR for default tolerance config (liam) - reconciler rule change (ana) - production rollout next week with post-deploy monitoring (raj + liam) - send a short notes to finance explaining why there will be a small transient ledger rewrite (sara)

liam: tagging this thread resolved — reopening if anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:
